l: thick darkness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Thick darkness covers the whole land after destruction, its vapor felt by surviving inhabitants. It prevents candles, torches, and fire from producing or showing light for three days, then disperses in the morning.

l: light, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_absent the whole land [no light at all] There was no light during the darkness: candles, torches, fire, the sun, the moon, and the stars could not be seen or provide light.

l: mourning, howling, and weeping, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: result_from the great and terrible destruction [and the darkness] Mourning, howling, and weeping occurred continually among the people during the three days of darkness because of the darkness and the great destruction.

l: the voice, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: A message heard among the people speaks again after silence, asking Israel how often it would gather them and calling them to repent and return.

l: people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: People of the earth, with fair sons and daughters, fall through iniquity; many are destroyed for wickedness, while survivors are called to receive Jesus Christ, repent, and convert.

l: the saints, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The saints are killed and shed blood through wickedness; their blood cries against wicked people, prompting destructions to end further bloodshed.

l: destruction, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_caused_by sin [because of wickedness and abominations] Many great destructions come upon the land and the people because of their wickedness and abominations. Cities are burned, sunk, covered with earth, or buried.

l: conversion, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_required_for healing [after repentance] The spared inhabitants are called to be converted. The Lamanites are described as having been converted through faith in Jesus Christ and baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost.

l: heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Heaven is where the Father’s will is done and holds incorruptible treasures secure from thieves. Jesus ascends there as disciples witness it; later three disciples are caught up there, see and hear unspeakable things, and are forbidden to speak of them.

l: sons of God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: are_given_to believers [by Jesus Christ] Jesus Christ gives those who receive him the opportunity to become the sons of God, and he will do the same for those who believe on his name.

l: light, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The eye is the body’s light: a single eye fills the body with light, while an evil eye fills it with darkness.

l: life, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Life is more than meat, the destination of the narrow way through the strait gate, found by few and promised eternally to those who endure to the end.

l: sacrifices, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jesus Christ commands that blood sacrifices and burnt offerings end, declaring that none will be accepted.

l: broken heart, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a sacrifice [accepted by Jesus Christ] Jesus Christ accepts a broken heart as a sacrifice. Whoever comes to him with a broken heart will be baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost.

l: contrite spirit, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a sacrifice [accepted by Jesus Christ] Jesus Christ accepts a contrite spirit as a sacrifice. Whoever comes to him with a contrite spirit will be baptized with fire and the Holy Ghost.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Holy Ghost is a power given by the Father, one with the Father and Jesus Christ, that bears record of both and manifests Jesus to the Gentiles. It is received through baptism in Jesus’s name by those who believe, repent, humble themselves, and come with a broken heart and contrite spirit. It comes with fire, fills those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, and sanctifies the repentant and baptized so they may stand spotless before Jesus at the last day. Jesus gives disciples power to give it, and it is given to believers through belief in Jesus’s words and the words of the disciples. It is poured out through Jesus Christ upon the Gentiles as a blessing, making them mighty unto the scattering of the people of the house of Israel.

l: sin, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Sin is what Jesus Christ saves the world from through redemption. People are urged to repent, and remission comes through baptism with humility and belief. Jesus also warns that lustful looking is adultery in the heart and commands such things not enter the heart.

l: childlike followers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: are_received_by Jesus Christ [as little children] Those who repent and come unto Jesus Christ as a little child will be received by him. Jesus Christ says that the kingdom of God belongs to such people.

l: death of Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jesus Christ’s death is signified beforehand, then he declares he laid down his life for childlike followers, was slain for the sins of the world, and lets people witness his wounds.

l: the people of Nephi who were spared, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The people of Nephi who were spared are a multitude gathered around the temple after Christ’s ascension. They marvel at a great change, converse about Jesus Christ, hear a voice from heaven, and see Jesus Christ descend. He shows them his body; they feel his wounds, worship him, and receive his doctrine. Jesus chooses the twelve to minister to them. Seated on earth, they receive bread and wine, eat and drink, are filled with the Holy Ghost, cry out with one voice, and give glory to Jesus Christ. They hear Jesus expound the scriptures and gather again to see and hear the children utter marvelous things.

l: the Lamanites who had been spared, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Lamanites who had been spared receive great favors and blessings as Christ manifests himself, shows his body, and ministers to them after ascending to heaven.

l: these sayings, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Sayings come to the Gentiles according to the Lord’s word, signaling that the covenant restoring the children of Israel is beginning to be fulfilled.

l: the covenant to their fathers, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_fulfilled the time of the fulfilling Its fulfilling is identified as the time until which the dwellings of the house of Israel may remain desolate.

l: the prophecies, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: are_fulfilled_by the deaths and destructions [through fire, smoke, tempests, whirlwinds, and the opening of the earth] The prophecies of many holy prophets concern the deaths and destructions by fire, smoke, tempests, whirlwinds, and the opening of the earth.

l: the deaths and destructions, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: They occur through fire, smoke, tempests, whirlwinds, and the opening of the earth to receive people. The text says they fulfill the prophecies of many holy prophets.

l: the ascension of Christ into heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The ascension is Jesus’s departure into heaven unto the Father. After showing himself to the multitude, healing, raising a man, and manifesting himself to spared Nephi and Lamanites, he touches disciples, is covered by a cloud, and ascends as they witness and bear record.

l: the mourning, weeping, and wailing, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The mourning, weeping, and wailing are made by people spared alive, cease after the earth stands again, and are transformed into joy, praise, and thanksgiving unto the Lord Jesus Christ.

l: silence, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: It remains in all the land for many hours because the people are astonished after hearing the sayings. The people later hear the voice again.

l: the blessing and favors shown to the spared people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Great favors are shown and great blessings are poured upon the heads of the spared people of Nephi and the spared Lamanites. Soon afterward, Christ manifests himself to them, shows them his body, and ministers to them.

l: the sins of the world, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: are_taken_upon_by Jesus Christ [through his suffering] Jesus Christ says that he has taken upon himself the sins of the world and suffered the will of the Father in all things from the beginning.

l: doctrine of Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The doctrine of Jesus Christ, given by Father, commands all people everywhere to repent and believe in Jesus Christ, be baptized, and become as a little child to receive salvation and the kingdom of God; it is a rock that withstands the gates of hell.

l: belief in Jesus Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Belief in Jesus Christ is commanded by the Father and required for baptism. With baptism it leads to the kingdom of God and salvation, brings the Holy Ghost, includes belief in the Father, and explains Jesus’s choice of disciples and his prayer for future believers.

l: the devil, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The devil, father of contention, entices and tempts people into captivity; Jesus commands watchfulness and prayer against being led away.

l: little child, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a_state_required_for kingdom of God [along with repentance and baptism] Jesus Christ teaches that people must become as a little child, repent, and be baptized in his name or they cannot receive these things or inherit the kingdom of God.

l: rock, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: supports house [as a foundation] The rock is the foundation of the house built by the wise man. The house does not fall because it is founded upon the rock.

l: earth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Earth is where the Father’s will is to be done, yet its treasures are vulnerable to corruption and theft; smitten with curse, it ends as heavens pass away and elements melt.

l: Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_served_by the law of Moses [all Israel] The children of Israel are the people concerning whom the Father made a covenant about restoration to the lands of their inheritance. The fulfillment of that covenant is already beginning when these sayings come to the Gentiles.

l: people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The people are taught to heed the twelve, believe in Jesus, repent, be baptized, reconcile with others, and show love through good works that glorify God.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The disciples are twelve ministers chosen by Jesus from among the people to serve this people and the multitude. They are given authority to baptize with water, testify of Jesus because they have seen and known him, teach the scriptures and his words, and minister the gospel sacrament of bread and wine. Jesus identifies them as his disciples and as a light to a people who are a remnant of the house of Joseph, commanding them to keep his commandments and rely on the Father in his name. He gives them power through ordination to give the Holy Ghost. After baptism, they receive the Holy Ghost and fire, are purified through faith, are ministered to by angels and Jesus, and become white as Jesus. They continue praying, teaching, baptizing in Jesus's name, distributing the sacrament, preaching what they have heard and seen, fasting and praying together, writing what they see and hear, and judging according to Jesus's judgment. Their ministry is built upon the gospel and extends to as many as come unto them.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The kingdom of heaven belongs to the poor in spirit who come unto Jesus and to those persecuted for his name’s sake. It is entered not by saying, Lord, Lord, but by doing the will of the Father and keeping Jesus’s commandments.

l: the commandments, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The commandments come from God and are given by Jesus. They call people to believe, repent, come with a broken heart and contrite spirit, and govern sacrament, prayer, worship, ministering, worthiness, and avoiding disputations; keeping them brings blessing and is required to enter the kingdom of heaven.

l: the gospel teachings, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: requires_love_for enemy [with blessing, good deeds, and prayer] The teachings in this unit call for humility, repentance, mercy, purity in heart, peacemaking, reconciliation, truthful speech, generosity, love of enemies, and prayer for persecutors. They teach that good works should lead people to glorify the Father in heaven.

l: the salt of the earth, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Salt of the earth must retain its savor; if it becomes unsavory, it is good for nothing, cast out, and trodden under foot.

l: the light of this people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The people are given light by Jesus, to shine through good works before others. Like an unhidden city on a hill, it is held up by disciples to the world, following Jesus so others glorify their Father in heaven.

l: judgment, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Judgment is measured according to the judgment people use and their works, calling people to correct themselves first. The Lord comes as a swift witness against wrongdoing, executes covenant justice, and will judge the world before the Father; disciples will judge people according to the judgment Jesus gives them.

l: men, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: receive what they would have done to themselves [under the golden rule] Men are taught to do to others what they would want others to do to them.

l: prayer, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Prayer is offered secretly to the Father without vain repetition, following a manner that hallows his name, seeks his will, forgiveness, and deliverance from evil.

l: temptation, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Temptation is something people enter by failing to watch and pray; Jesus warns that the devil and Satan can lead them into it.

l: treasures, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Earthly treasures face corruption and theft; treasures laid up in heaven are secure, and a person's heart follows the person's treasure.

l: Mammon, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a master [in conflict with God] Mammon is a master that cannot be served together with God. A person will hate one master and love the other, or hold to one and despise the other.

l: the day of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The day of the Lord is a great, dreadful day: Elijah is sent before it; the proud and wicked burn like an oven, leaving neither root nor branch, while the righteous tread them down.

l: the multitude, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The multitude disperses after Jesus ascends, regathers to see him, divides into twelve bodies, is taught and led in prayer by disciples, follows them to water, witnesses the Holy Ghost and fire, and understands Jesus's words in their hearts.

l: asking, seeking, and knocking, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: receives given answers [according to the respective request] Asking, seeking, and knocking are associated with receiving, finding, and having the way opened. Jesus teaches that the Father gives good things to them that ask him.

l: bread, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: represents the body of Jesus Christ [to the soul of the eater] Jesus Christ breaks and blesses bread, gives it to the disciples, and commands the disciples to give it to the multitude. He teaches that whoever eats this bread eats of his body to the soul.

l: the law and the prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_summarized_by golden rule [as its principle] The law and the prophets are identified with the teaching that men should do to others as they would want others to do to them.

l: golden rule, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The golden rule is stated as doing to men whatever one would want men to do to oneself.

l: strait gate, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The strait gate is the entrance to the narrow way leading unto life; Jesus commands people to enter through it, though few find it.

l: broad way, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The broad way is wide, entered and traveled by many, leading from its open entrance toward destruction and death until night comes.

l: false prophets, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: False prophets wear sheep’s clothing, are inwardly ravening wolves, and are revealed by their fruits.

l: fruits, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: reveals false prophets [by their quality] Fruits reveal what kind of tree produces them and allow people to know false prophets. Good fruit comes from a good tree, while evil fruit comes from a corrupt tree.

l: good tree, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: A good tree consistently produces good fruit, cannot produce evil fruit, and is cut down and put into fire without good fruit.

l: corrupt tree, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: A corrupt tree consistently produces evil fruit, cannot produce good fruit, and is hewn down and cast into the fire.

l: house, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: A house is founded on rock when its builder hears and does Jesus’s sayings, withstanding rain, floods, and winds; founded on sand when its builder hears but does not do them, it falls.

l: sand, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: supports house [as an unstable foundation] The sand is the foundation of the house built by the foolish man. The house falls when rain, floods, and winds beat upon it.

l: fall of the house, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_great great [after the house falls] The fall of the house occurs when the foolish man’s house, built upon sand, is beaten by rain, floods, and winds. Its fall is described as great.

l: Moses, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a servant [of the Lord] Moses is identified as the Lord’s servant. The law was commanded to him in Horeb for all Israel.

l: the house of Joseph, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: has_remnant the twelve disciples A remnant of the house of Joseph is the people among whom the twelve disciples are a light. The Father gave their land of inheritance to them.

l: the other tribes of the house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Other tribes of the house of Israel are led away and separated because of iniquity; unknown to Jerusalem and the twelve disciples, they remain known to the Father.

l: the other sheep, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The other sheep are Jesus’s sheep outside the twelve disciples’ fold; Jesus must bring them, they will hear his voice, and are identified as the twelve disciples.

l: the fold, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: has the other sheep [the other sheep are not of it] The fold is understood by the disciples as referring to their group, but Jesus teaches that other sheep are not of this fold and will also be brought into one fold.

l: the shepherd, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jesus teaches that there shall be one fold and one shepherd.

l: the Gentiles, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Gentiles are a group addressed throughout the records as recipients of the gospel, Jesus’s teachings, and the Holy Ghost. They are to be converted through the preaching of the disciples rather than hearing Jesus’s voice directly, except through the Holy Ghost. Because of belief in Jesus, they are blessed and receive witness, truth, and eventually the fulness of the gospel, while the house of Israel is scattered. They become mighty and are associated with the scattering of the house of Israel, yet this blessing carries a warning: rejecting the fulness, hardening their hearts, or continuing in pride, lyings, deceits, murder, priestcraft, whoredoms, secret abominations, and other wickedness brings judgment, destruction, and being cut off. Works, writings, and sayings are to come forth from or through them as signs and as a means of bringing again what Jesus taught; a great and marvelous work is also to occur among them before the judgment day. Their path remains conditional: they are commanded to repent, come unto Jesus Christ, be baptized in his name, receive remission of sins and the Holy Ghost, know his doctrine, and thereby be numbered with the house of Israel. They may then assist the remnant of Jacob; otherwise their iniquities return upon their own heads. They are also said to be inherited by the woman's seed.

l: other sheep, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Other sheep are outside Jerusalem and surrounding lands, have not yet heard or seen Jesus, but he will go to them so they hear his voice and are numbered among his sheep.

l: Isaiah, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Isaiah, whose great words concern Israel, Zion, and Gentiles, prophesies of Zion in words fulfilled afterward and is to be searched diligently.

l: Zion, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_established_among house of Israel [when Israel is gathered from dispersion] Zion will be established again among the house of Israel when the dispersed people are gathered.

l: the gospel of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The gospel of Christ is the fulness given by Jesus and preached to the people of Nephi, the Gentiles, and the remnant of Jacob. Jesus teaches that he came to do the Father’s will, was lifted up upon the cross, and draws all men to judgment according to their works; those in the church are to do the works they have seen him do. The three disciples preach it broadly, converting those who accept it and uniting them to the church of Christ. Its fulness is manifested to the Gentiles and then brought to the house of Israel: hardened, rejecting Gentiles lose it, while repentant Gentiles are numbered among Israel. It then begins the Father’s work among the remnant of Jacob and the dispersed house of Israel.

l: knowledge of Jesus and the gospel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The written sayings are to help the people at Jerusalem and other tribes receive knowledge through the Holy Ghost. The remnant of the house of Israel may be brought to a knowledge of Jesus, and the house of Israel will come to knowledge of the fulness of the gospel.

l: Jesus's voice, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The other sheep have not yet heard Jesus’s voice, but Jesus will go to them so they shall hear it. Those who hear and are numbered among his sheep will be part of one fold with one shepherd.

l: the multitude, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The multitude, about two thousand five hundred men, women, and children, listens to Jesus, brings sick, afflicted people and little children, worships him, bears record of his prayer, and sees and hears angels minister to the children.

l: the sick and afflicted people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: are_healed_by Jesus [when brought forth to him] The sick and afflicted people are brought to Jesus, including those who are lame, blind, halt, maimed, leprous, withered, deaf, dumb, or afflicted in any manner. Jesus heals every one of them as they are brought forth.

l: the little children, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The little children are brought to Jesus, blessed and prayed for one by one, as fiery angels encircle and minister.

l: healing the afflicted, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jesus invites the sick and afflicted people to come to him because he has compassion and mercy. He heals every one of them as they are brought forth.

l: Jesus's prayer to the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: causes joy [in the souls of the multitude] Jesus kneels upon the earth and prays unto the Father, but the things he prays cannot be written. The multitude bears record that they heard great and marvelous things and felt joy as he prayed for them.

l: the children's blessing, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jesus takes the little children one by one, blesses them, and prays unto the Father for them. Afterward, he tells the multitude to behold their little ones as angels descend and minister unto them.

l: joy, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The multitude is filled with joy while Jesus prays for them and is overcome after he finishes praying. Jesus says that his joy is full, and he weeps.

l: the people of Jesus's church, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Believers baptized in Jesus's name repent, receive bread and wine, meet, pray for others, and avoid disputations.

l: bread, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_part_of the gospel sacrament [in remembrance of Jesus's body] Jesus takes bread, breaks and blesses it, gives it to the disciples, and commands them to eat and give it to the multitude. Bread is administered in remembrance of Jesus's body.

l: wine, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Wine is a gospel sacrament representing Jesus Christ’s blood to the drinker’s soul. Jesus commands disciples to drink it from the cup and give it to the multitude, administering it in remembrance of his blood.

l: Jesus's body, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_remembered_by the gospel sacrament [through bread] Jesus commands the people to eat bread in remembrance of his body, which he has shown to them.

l: blood of Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Blood of Jesus is shed for people, remembered through wine in a gospel sacrament, and washes garments as people exercise faith, repent of sins, and remain faithful to the end.

l: Jesus's flesh, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_partaken_of_in the gospel sacrament [by worthy participants] Jesus teaches that those who knowingly eat his flesh unworthily eat damnation to their souls. Those known to be unworthy are to be forbidden from partaking, while still being ministered to and prayed for.

l: Jesus's Spirit, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_received_by believers [when they always remember Jesus] Jesus teaches that those who always remember him will have his Spirit with them.

l: the gospel sacrament, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_for_remembrance_of Jesus [of his body and blood] The text describes bread and wine being broken, blessed, eaten, and drunk in remembrance of Jesus's body and blood, and commands this practice to continue.

l: the Holy Ghost ordination, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: gives_power_to the disciples [to give the Holy Ghost] Jesus touches the chosen disciples one by one and gives them power to give the Holy Ghost.

l: Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Nephi, a disciple chosen by Jesus, is baptized in water and then baptizes all disciples Jesus had chosen.

l: the people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: have all things [in common] The people were taught by Jesus, and some of them were baptized and filled with the Holy Ghost. They taught and ministered one to another, had all things common, dealt justly, and did all things Jesus commanded.

l: Jesus's ministering, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_received_by the disciples [after the angels ministered] Jesus ministers unto the disciples after angels minister to them. He also teaches the multitude, commands them and the disciples to pray, blesses the disciples, and speaks of the great things they have seen and heard.

l: purification, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_in Jesus [through faith on Jesus's words] Jesus says that the disciples have been purified because of their faith. He prays that those who believe on the disciples' words may also be purified in him and that he may be glorified in them.

l: house of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The house of Israel is a scattered people of the covenant, including remnants across the earth. Jesus Christ completes the Father’s commandment concerning them. They will be gathered from east, west, south, and north, brought to know the Lord their God, redeemed, and receive their inheritance. Repentant people who hearken will be numbered among them, and Gentiles may join after remission of sins and receiving the Holy Ghost. They will be established in a New Jerusalem and blessed through covenant fulfillment.

l: the remnant of the house of Jacob, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The remnant of the house of Jacob is a remnant of the house of Israel among the Gentiles, dwelling as a lion among beasts and sheep. It receives this land from the Father, goes forth with power over adversaries, whose enemies are cut off, and assists repentant Gentiles and the house of Israel to build New Jerusalem and gather the dispersed people.

l: Abraham, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_ancestor_of the house of Israel [through the covenant] Abraham received the covenant that in his seed all the kindreds of the earth would be blessed. The Father fulfills this covenant through the blessing of the people and the pouring out of the Holy Ghost through Jesus Christ upon the Gentiles.

l: New Jerusalem, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: New Jerusalem is the promised land and a city for the scattered house of Israel. The Father establishes the people there, with the powers of heaven and Jesus Christ in their midst. The remnant of Jacob, the house of Israel, and assistants build it as dispersed people gather into it.

l: the sacrament of bread and wine, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: fills the multitude [with the Spirit] The bread and wine are given and consumed by the disciples and the multitude. Jesus Christ teaches that the bread is his body and the wine is his blood to the soul, and those who eat and drink shall never hunger or thirst but shall be filled.

l: the scattering of Israel, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_caused_by the Gentiles [after the Gentiles receive a blessing] The Gentiles receive a blessing through the Holy Ghost that makes them mighty above all, unto the scattering of the people of the house of Israel. They are also described as a scourge unto the people of the land.

l: salvation, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Jerusalem will be redeemed without money, and the people will know the name of Jesus Christ. The people will announce peace and salvation, and Jerusalem will be inhabited again with the people as the land of their inheritance.

l: the servant, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The servant will declare the work among the Gentiles and bring forth Jesus Christ’s words with power, be marred because of them, and be healed by Jesus Christ.

l: the work of the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The work of the Father, a great and marvelous work among the Gentiles, commences among the remnant of Jacob as the gospel is preached, prepares people to come to Jesus Christ, and gathers Israel from all nations to its inheritance.

l: building the New Jerusalem, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_done_by remnant of Jacob [with assistance from Gentiles and the house of Israel] The remnant of Jacob and the house of Israel will build a city called the New Jerusalem. Those who repent and are numbered among the remnant will assist in the building.

l: sin and corruption, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_done_away lyings, deceivings, envyings, strifes, priestcrafts, and whoredoms [at that day] Lyings, deceivings, envyings, strifes, priestcrafts, and whoredoms will be done away. Witchcrafts, soothsayers, graven images, standing images, and the works of people’s hands will be cut off.

l: New Jerusalem gathering, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: gathers my people [from across the face of the land] The people scattered across the land will be gathered into the New Jerusalem. The power of heaven will come down among them, and Jesus Christ will be in their midst.

l: woman (the Lord's wife), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Lord’s wife is a once-barren, forsaken, grieved, refused wife of youth with children and seed. The Lord promises her restoration: an enlarged tent and habitations, freedom from remembered shame and widowhood’s reproach, establishment in righteousness, and safety far from oppression and terror.

l: children (the woman's children), The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The woman's children become more numerous than the married wife's children, inherit the Gentiles, receive the Lord's teaching, and enjoy great peace.

l: the Lord's kindness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Lord's everlasting kindness remains with the woman, enduring even beyond mountains and hills.

l: the Lord's mercy, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Great, everlasting mercy is promised and shown to the woman as the Lord gathers her with kindness.

l: the Lord's covenant of peace, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_not_removed woman (the Lord's wife) The Lord's covenant of peace will not be removed from the woman.

l: weapon, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: does_not_prosper woman (the Lord's wife) [when formed against her] No weapon formed against the Lord's servants will prosper.

l: servants of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Lord’s servants receive heritage and righteousness: weapons against them fail, and reviling tongues are condemned.

l: saints, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Many saints arose from the dead, appeared and ministered to Jesus’ people; Jesus commanded the previously omitted event be recorded.

l: the record, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_kept_by Nephi Jesus commands Nephi to bring forth the record he has kept. After learning that the rising and ministering of many saints was not recorded, Jesus commands that it be written in the record.

l: words, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: go_forth_to Gentiles [according to the time and will of the Father] Jesus commands the people to give heed to his words and says that those who hearken to his words, repent, and are baptized shall be saved. The words spoken by Isaiah have been and shall be fulfilled.

l: Malachi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: receives_words_from the Father [to tell them to others] Malachi is the one to whom the Father gives words that are written and later expounded.

l: the messenger, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The messenger, sent by the Father, prepares his way, comes suddenly to the temple, and purifies Levi’s sons.

l: the messenger of the covenant, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The messenger of the covenant, whom people delight in, suddenly comes to the temple.

l: the day of his coming, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The day of his coming is hard to endure, refining and purifying those present like fire and soap.

l: return to the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_answered_by return to you [the Lord of Hosts promises reciprocal return] The people are told to return to the Lord, with the promise that he will return to them.

l: tithes, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Tithes are owed to the Lord of Hosts, withheld as robbery, and must be brought into the storehouse.

l: offerings, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Offerings owed to the Lord of Hosts are withheld, robbing God, until Judah and Jerusalem’s offering again becomes pleasant.

l: a blessing, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_poured_out the nation [from the windows of heaven, beyond sufficient room to receive] The Lord promises to open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing so abundant that there will not be room enough to receive it.

l: the ordinances, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The people have gone away from the ordinances of their fathers and have not kept them.

l: righteousness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_discerned_from wickedness [by those who return] The sons of Levi will be purified so that they may offer an offering to the Lord in righteousness.

l: service to God, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Service to God is called vain and unprofitable by some, who question the benefit of keeping ordinances and walking mournfully before the Lord of Hosts.

l: Son of Righteousness, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: arises healing [in his wings] The Son of Righteousness will arise for those who fear the Lord’s name, bringing healing in his wings.

l: Elijah the prophet, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Elijah the prophet is sent before the Lord’s great and dreadful day, turning fathers’ hearts to children and children’s hearts to fathers.

l: the children, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: speak_to their fathers [great and marvelous things] Jesus taught and ministered to the children of the multitude and loosed their tongues. The children, including babes, uttered great and marvelous things that were forbidden to be written.

l: resurrection of everlasting life, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_for the people [if their works are good] Those whose works are good shall come forth to the resurrection of everlasting life.

l: resurrection of damnation, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_for the people [if their works are evil] Those whose works are evil shall come forth to the resurrection of damnation.

l: the greater things, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The greater things will be made manifest to people who believe the things first given; disbelief causes them to be withheld unto condemnation.

l: the things Jesus taught, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: are_brought_again_to the people [from the Gentiles] Only a hundredth part of the things Jesus taught could be written in the book. The plates of Nephi contain the more part of his teachings, while Mormon wrote a lesser part.

l: three days of teaching, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: is_a teaching [by Jesus to the people] Jesus truly taught the people for the space of three days.

l: people, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The people dispute about the name of the church, and the works of the people are to be written. Their works will be known through the books and will be part of their judgment.

l: name of Jesus, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The name of Jesus is the name by which the church must be called and by which people must take upon themselves his name. The Father will hear and answer prayers made in this name.

l: cross, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: draws men [through Jesus being lifted up] Jesus is sent by the Father to be lifted up upon the cross. After being lifted up, he draws all men unto him so they can be judged according to their works.

l: books, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: make_known works [to men] The books that have been written and will be written contain records by which the works of the people and the world will be known and judged. All things are written by the Father.

l: generation, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: has_no_lost_members none [the generation then alive] Jesus says that he, the Father, and the holy angels rejoice because none of the people of this generation are lost. He says that this generation gives him fulness of joy.

l: fourth generation, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The fourth generation causes Jesus sorrow: led captive, its people sell him for silver, gold, and corruptible or stolen things; their works return upon themselves.

l: narrow way, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: leads_to life [few find it] The narrow way leads to life, and few people find it.

l: death, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Death is reached through the broad way, which many people travel. The three disciples are promised that they will never taste of death and will not endure its pains. Mormon learns that a change was necessary so they would not taste death.

l: the disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The disciples ask Jesus for their ministry to end after reaching the age of man so they may come to him in his kingdom; he promises that at seventy-two years old they will come to him and find rest.

l: the three disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The three disciples desire to bring souls to Jesus while the world stands. They never taste death and are changed to immortality when Jesus comes in glory. In their changed state they have no pain, sorrow except for the sins of the world, and fulness of joy; they are as angels of God, see and hear unspeakable things in heaven, and are forbidden to utter them. They unite the church of Christ, receive no harm, remain hidden while among Gentiles and Jews, minister to scattered Israel and all peoples, and bring souls to Jesus. They may show themselves, work great and marvelous works, and remain until Christ’s judgment day.

l: the people of Nephi, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The people of Nephi receive Christ’s gospel from three disciples, are converted to the Lord, unite with Christ’s church, and are blessed according to Jesus’s word.

l: the kingdom of the Father, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The disciples who desire to end their ministry are promised rest with Jesus in his kingdom. The three disciples will have fulness of joy, sit in the kingdom of the Father, and at the judgment day be received into it eternally.

l: immortality, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The three disciples are changed from mortality toward an immortal state and are sanctified in the flesh. Their change is not equal to the greater change that will take place at the last day.

l: the change wrought upon the three disciples, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The change wrought upon the three disciples sanctifies them in the flesh, shielding them from pain, sorrow, Satan’s temptations, and earthly powers until they receive a greater change at the judgment day of Christ.

l: the judgment day of Christ, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: Before it, three disciples perform great and marvelous works and bring many souls to Jesus; at the judgment day of Christ they receive a greater change and enter the Father’s kingdom eternally.

l: the words of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: The Lord’s words, spoken by holy prophets, will all be fulfilled and are neither vain nor delayed.

l: the doings of the Lord, The Third Book of Nephi, the Son of Nephi, Who Was the Son of Helaman
s: are_spurned the children of Israel [when these sayings come forth among them] The doings of the Lord should not be spurned, denied, hissed at, or made game of. Those who spurn them will be overtaken by the sword of his justice.

l: The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The people were converted unto the Lord and lived in peace, sharing their goods and receiving blessings, while the disciples of Jesus performed miracles. The people of Nephi prospered, rebuilt cities, and became rich, but later pride, divisions, churches, wickedness, and secret combinations spread among them and the Lamanites. The Nephites and Lamanites became exceedingly wicked, while the disciples of Jesus remained righteous and continued to suffer persecution. Nephi, Amos, and Ammaron kept the records, and Ammaron hid the sacred records after three hundred and twenty years from the coming of Christ.

l: Jesus, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: Jesus was the one in whose name the disciples worked miracles. The people who believed in Jesus were called true believers and true worshipers of Christ.

l: the disciples of Jesus, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The disciples of Jesus formed a church of Christ, baptized those who repented, and saw them receive the Holy Ghost. They healed the sick, raised the dead, and performed many other miracles in the name of Jesus. The disciples who remained were persecuted, imprisoned, cast into furnaces and dens of wild beasts, and continued doing miracles without being harmed.

l: the church of Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The disciples of Jesus formed a church of Christ in all the surrounding lands. The true church was later denied and persecuted by other churches, while its disciples remained humble and believed in Christ.

l: the people of Nephi, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The people of Nephi were converted unto the Lord, became strong, multiplied, and became fair and delightsome. They rebuilt cities, including Zarahemla, and were blessed in marriage and according to the Lord’s promises. Later, they became proud because of their riches and became exceedingly wicked like the Lamanites.

l: the Lamanites, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The Lamanites were converted unto the Lord with the Nephites, and there was peace between them. Later, some people took upon themselves the name of Lamanites, and the Lamanites became proud, wicked, and taught their children to reject the gospel of Christ.

l: Nephites, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The true believers in Christ were called Nephites, along with Jacobites, Josephites, and Zoramites. The Nephites later became exceedingly wicked like the Lamanites.

l: the children of Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The people who were in one and free from robbers, murderers, and divisions were called the children of Christ and heirs to the kingdom of God.

l: the people, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The people were converted, had all things common, dealt justly, and lived without contention for many years. Later, they became divided into classes, built churches for gain, and became increasingly wicked.

l: the wicked part of the people, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The wicked part of the people became more numerous and stronger than the people of God. They built churches, adorned them with precious things, and later built up the secret oaths and combinations of Gadianton.

l: the robbers of Gadianton, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The robbers of Gadianton spread over all the land after three hundred years had passed away. They trafficked in all manner of traffic and laid up gold and silver in abundance.

l: Nephi, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: Nephi kept the last record upon the plates of Nephi. He died after the first generation from Christ had passed away, and his son Amos kept the record in his stead.

l: Amos, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: Amos kept the record upon the plates of Nephi for eighty-four years after Nephi died. Amos later died, and his son Amos kept the record; that Amos eventually died after three hundred and five years had passed away.

l: Ammaron, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: Ammaron kept the record after his brother Amos died. Constrained by the Holy Ghost, he hid up the sacred records after three hundred and twenty years had passed away.

l: the land, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The land had no contention during the people’s period of peace, and cities were rebuilt where cities had been burned. Some cities had been sunk and could not be renewed. Later, the land was filled with many churches, wickedness, and robbers of Gadianton.

l: the plates of Nephi, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: Nephi kept the last record upon the plates of Nephi. Amos and his son Amos also kept the record upon the plates of Nephi.

l: the records, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The records were handed down from generation to generation and included sacred records. Ammaron hid them up unto the Lord so they could come again unto the remnant of the house of Jacob.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: Those who repented and were baptized received the Holy Ghost. The Holy Ghost constrained Ammaron to hide up the sacred records.

l: the gospel of Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The people who rejected the gospel of Christ were called Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites. They wilfully rebelled against it and taught their children not to believe.

l: the conversion of the people, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: In the thirty and sixth year, all the people across the land, both Nephites and Lamanites, were converted unto the Lord. They had no contentions or disputations and dealt justly with one another.

l: peace, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: Peace continued in the land for many years, and there was no contention among the people because of the love of God in their hearts. Peace later remained for a small part of the people even after some revolted from the church.

l: miracles, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The disciples of Jesus performed great and marvelous works, including healing the sick, raising the dead, and causing the lame, blind, and deaf to receive healing. They worked miracles only in the name of Jesus, and their miracles continued despite persecution.

l: the coming of Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The records mark the passing of years from the coming of Christ. Ammaron hid the sacred records in the three hundred and twentieth year from the coming of Christ.

l: the love of God, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The love of God dwelled in the hearts of the people and caused there to be no contention in the land.

l: the churches that professed to know Christ, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: Many churches professed to know Christ while denying most parts of his gospel. They received all manner of wickedness and administered sacred things to those forbidden to receive them because of unworthiness.

l: the riches of the people, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The people became exceedingly rich because of their prosperity in Christ. Their riches led some to pride, costly apparel, fine pearls, division into classes, and the building of churches for gain.

l: the division among the people, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: In the two hundred and thirty and first year, there was a great division among the people. The true believers were called Nephites, Jacobites, Josephites, and Zoramites, while those who rejected the gospel were called Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites.

l: the records hidden by Ammaron, The Fourth Book of Nephi, Who Is the Son of Nephi, One of the Disciples of Jesus Christ
s: The records hidden by Ammaron were sacred records handed down from generation to generation. Ammaron hid them unto the Lord so they might come again unto the remnant of the house of Jacob according to the Lord’s prophecies and promises.

l: The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: These chapters present Mormon’s record of the Nephites’ final decline, destruction, and continuing witness of Jesus Christ. As a youth, Mormon is instructed by Ammaron to observe events and later retrieve the plates of Nephi at hill Shim. Though Mormon is visited by the Lord and tastes the goodness of Jesus, he is forbidden to preach because widespread wickedness, unbelief, and hardened hearts dominate the land. He becomes a military leader as the Nephites repeatedly fight the Lamanites, lose cities and lands, make temporary treaties, and persist in sorrow without true repentance. After the Nephites vow vengeance, Mormon refuses to lead them, warning that all people will stand before the judgment-seat of Christ. War intensifies around Desolation and Teancum. The Lamanites defeat the Nephites, take prisoners, and sacrifice Nephite women and children to idol gods. Mormon retrieves the hidden records, later returns to command the Nephite armies, and records their destruction as the Lamanites overwhelm them. He explains that the record is intended for the remnant, the Gentiles, Jews, and the house of Israel, warning against unbelief, idolatry, and wickedness while affirming God’s covenants and the prayers of the righteous. At Cumorah, nearly all remaining Nephites are killed. Mormon hides the sacred records, gives a few plates to Moroni, and mourns the dead, teaching that all will become immortal and face Christ in judgment. He addresses the remnant of the house of Israel, urging repentance, peace, belief in Jesus Christ, and baptism. Moroni completes Mormon’s record, hides it in the earth, and prophesies its future coming forth amid unbelief, pride, and exploitation. The final message affirms that God is unchanging and performs miracles, calls disciples to preach, promises salvation to believers, acknowledges the record’s imperfections, and prays for restoration and fulfillment of God’s covenant with the house of Israel.

l: The Book of Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_a record Mormon calls his record of the things he has seen and heard the Book of Mormon.

l: Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Mormon is a Nephite, descendant of Nephi, record keeper, commander, and witness of things seen and heard by the Spirit. Visited by the Lord at fifteen and knowing the goodness of Jesus through personal experience, he is forbidden to preach because of his people’s rebellion. Young and large in stature, he is appointed to lead the Nephite armies and repeatedly leads them in battle while recording their wickedness, abominations, and destruction. He loves the Nephites with all his heart and continually prays for them, yet loses hope because he knows the Lord’s judgments. He refuses for a time to command them because of their wickedness, standing as an idle witness, then returns to lead them after repenting of his oath. Following Ammaron’s words, he takes the plates from hill Shim, makes records, and writes a small abridgment for the seed of Jacob, Gentiles, and all the ends of the earth. As the Lamanites overthrow the land, he gathers the Nephites at Cumorah, hides the entrusted records, gives plates to Moroni, leads his ten thousand in battle, survives wounded, and mourns the slain.

l: Ammaron, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Ammaron is a person who deposits and hides sacred records and engravings unto the Lord at hill Shim in Antum, then instructs Mormon to retrieve Nephi’s plates at twenty-four and engrave observations about the people.

l: Mormon, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Mormon, Moroni’s father, makes a record, commands Moroni to finish it, then is killed with their kinsfolk in battle.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Jesus Christ is identified as God, Lord and Savior, Christ, the Son of God, the Lamb of God, and the Father and the Son; he is the Father’s beloved. He chooses twelve disciples in Jerusalem, performs mighty miracles, gives his disciples the gospel commission, and promises salvation and signs to those who believe in his name and are baptized. He receives repentant people and Nephites with open arms, though the fallen Nephites reject him. He is slain by Jews, then raised by the Father’s power, gaining victory over death and bringing resurrection of the dead and redemption of the world. He will judge the house of Israel according to works. He also shows Moroni people of a future day and their actions. Mormon, at fifteen, tastes and knows his goodness.

l: Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Lord is a deity and God of the Nephites whose actions respond to the people’s righteousness or wickedness. He receives sacred records and engravings, visits Mormon, commands Mormon and later Moroni concerning the records, and preserves them from falling into Lamanite hands. Because of Nephite iniquity, he takes away beloved disciples, ends miracles and healing, withholds happiness and strength, and curses the land. Yet he is merciful and long-suffering, giving Mormon hope and calling the Nephites to repent, come unto him, be baptized, and build up his church so they may be spared. When they fail to repent and depart from his ways, he judges them, claims vengeance, and brings destruction. He remembers covenants, brings records out of darkness, and continues his eternal purposes and promises until fulfilled.

l: the Holy Ghost, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: God, one with the Father and the Son, comes not upon wicked unbelievers; believers are baptized with the Holy Ghost after water.

l: Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Nephites are a people, one of two parties, consisting of the Jacobites, Josephites, and Zoramites. They possess lands, arms, strongholds, towns, villages, and cities, and initially gather more than thirty thousand men. They win several battles against the Lamanites, prepare and fortify their lands, and maintain cities under Mormon’s command. Yet they continually persist in wickedness, bloodshed, boasting, and refusal to repent or call upon God. Although they sometimes defeat larger armies, they are repeatedly frightened, driven from cities and lands, weakened, divided, slaughtered, and swept off. Their women and children are taken prisoner and sacrificed. In their final struggle, they gather with wives and children at Cumorah; nearly all are slain, with only twenty and four surviving alongside Mormon, while others escape or desert. Those who escape are hunted from place to place until destroyed. Their destruction through Lamanite conquest is nearly complete and follows their departure from the ways of the Lord and rejection of Jesus Christ.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Lamanites are a people made up of Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites, one of two parties and enemies of the Nephites. They have their own lands, exceed the Nephites in number, and include Gadianton robbers among them. They fight near Zarahemla, attack with great power, drive the Nephites northward, and gain the land southward by treaty. Though defeated at city Desolation with many slain, they repeatedly invade, capture cities and prisoners, sacrifice Nephite women and children, and gain continuing power. They ultimately overcome the Nephites, burn and destroy their towns, villages, cities, and remaining inhabitants. After allowing the gathering at Cumorah, their armies kill nearly all of Mormon's people, hunt the survivors until none remain, and are also at war among themselves.

l: the Gadianton robbers, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Gadianton robbers are robbers among the Lamanites who infest the land, contribute to wickedness and destruction, fight the Nephites, and later join the Lamanites in a treaty dividing lands of inheritance.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_covered_with buildings [across the whole face of the land] Zarahemla is the land to which Mormon is carried by his father when he is eleven years old. War between the Nephites and Lamanites begins in its borders by the waters of Sidon.

l: hill Shim, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Hill Shim in Antum is where Mormon retrieves Ammaron’s hidden records as the Lamanites threaten to overthrow the land.

l: the land, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The land fills with buildings and people, is cursed for hardened hearts, makes treasures slippery, and becomes a place of sorceries, witchcrafts, and magics.

l: records, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Ammaron deposits and hides the records unto the Lord at hill Shim, then tells Mormon where they are; later Mormon takes them up as the Lamanites near overthrowing the land.

l: plates of Nephi, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Plates of Nephi are taken by Mormon at Ammaron’s command. Mormon engraves his observations concerning the people on them, making a record that contains a full account of their wickedness and abominations.

l: the Book of Mormon record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Book of Mormon record contains Mormon’s account of what he saw, heard, and observed concerning the people. Mormon made it, Moroni finished it, and it was hidden in the earth. Though imperfect in language and manner of speech, it is of great worth, written in reformed Egyptian, and will come to light by God’s power to bring knowledge of Christ and greater things to those who receive it without condemnation.

l: the people, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The people become almost as numerous as the sand of the sea, hide treasures from Gadianton robbers, and grow wicked and unbelieving until gifts, healing, and Mormon’s preaching cease.

l: the war between the Nephites and Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: A war between the Nephites and Lamanites begins in Zarahemla, by the waters of Sidon. The Nephites first win several battles, but war soon resumes and brings repeated attacks, retreats, destruction, and a treaty dividing the lands. After ten years, the Lamanites return to battle and are defeated again; the Nephites vow vengeance for their slain brethren. Over many further years, thousands die on both sides as the Lamanites increasingly defeat and drive back the Nephites, who gain no further power over them.

l: peace, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Peace is established in the land after the Lamanites withdraw their design and lasts about four years without bloodshed.

l: wickedness, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Wickedness is evil and abominable conduct that prevails throughout the land among the Nephites. It brings unbelief, sorceries, witchcrafts, and magics; prevents gifts from the Lord; and causes the Lord to take away beloved disciples. It fills the land throughout Mormon’s life, causing him continual sorrow. As the people remain hard-hearted and refuse repentance, Mormon refuses further command, the Lord declares they will be cut off, and wickedness stirs up bloodshed of unprecedented extent.

l: unbelief and idolatry, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: causes Nephites [to become a dark, filthy, and loathsome people] The seed of the people becomes dark, filthy, and loathsome because of unbelief and idolatry. The Spirit of the Lord has ceased to strive with their fathers, who are without Christ and God in the world.

l: God, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: God is a deity, creator, and the Nephites’ Lord, with all power over earth and humanity and knowledge of all things. He created heaven, earth, Adam, the Nephites, and all things in them; he is Jesus’s Father, answers prayer according to faith, and raises all men at the sounding of the trump. He spared the Nephites and granted repentance, while Mormon prayed to him for them. He leads his people, remembers covenants and righteous prayers, gives words and power for the record and mighty works, and may command war. He acts justly against the unrepentant and remains unchangeable and miraculous forever.

l: armies of the Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Nephite armies retreat, defend fortified cities, and battle under Mormon, sometimes defeating larger forces before losing the strength of the Lord.

l: armies of the Lamanites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Armies of the Lamanites, greater in number than the Nephites, march toward and attack them, driving them from cities and lands. Though defeated by Mormon’s forces and later making a treaty, they continue and leave nearly all Nephites dead.

l: Shem, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Shem is a land where the Nephites are driven after fleeing northward. Mormon fortifies its city and gathers the Nephites there in an effort to save them from destruction.

l: treaty between the Nephites, Lamanites, and robbers of Gadianton, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: A treaty among Nephites, Lamanites, and robbers of Gadianton divides lands of inheritance: Nephites receive northward land to the narrow passage, Lamanites southward land.

l: destruction, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_caused_by wickedness and abominations [as a consequence of the people's conduct] Destruction hangs over the people because of their wickedness, robbers, murders, magic art, and witchcraft. Mormon sees thousands of Nephites hewn down in rebellion and heaped upon the land.

l: blood and carnage, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Horrible blood and carnage spread among Nephites and Lamanites, escalating into a complete revolution throughout the land.

l: mourning and lamentation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Mourning and lamentation spread throughout the land, especially among Nephites unable to keep possessions; Mormon first rejoices, then recognizes sorrow lacks true repentance.

l: repentance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Repentance is required for salvation and for being spared by the Lord, and God requires it of the Gentiles. The Nephites begin with sorrow and crying, yet fail to repent through God’s goodness or come to Jesus with broken hearts and contrite spirits. Though the Lord calls them to repent after deliverance, they harden their hearts; destruction and being cut off follow. Mormon laments that repentance could have prevented their fall. The records command people to repent of every sin, turn from evil, humble themselves, resist temptation, and serve God.

l: Gentiles, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Gentiles are people addressed by Mormon who scatter the Nephites and possess their land. They receive reserved blessings and the gospel, are to care for the house of Israel, and must repent and humble themselves before God. A record comes to them from the Jews and then to the remnant.

l: house of Israel, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The house of Israel is a people, a house, and the covenant people of the Lord. It has a land of inheritance given by the Lord their God and a covenant with Abraham and Israel. It will be judged according to its works by the twelve chosen by Jesus in Jerusalem, and is called to prepare to return to its inheritance. Though it will suffer calamity, destruction, driving, and scattering, the Lord will remember the covenant. Its remnant is identified, Gentiles care for it, and God the Father is asked to bless it forever through faith on Jesus Christ.

l: remnant of this people, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The remnant of this people, spared and part of the house of Israel, is addressed to learn of its fathers. To be saved, it must repent, abandon weapons and shedding blood, believe in Jesus Christ, be baptized, and lay hold on the gospel of Christ.

l: land Desolation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Land containing the city of Desolation, where Mormon gathers Nephites for defense; their armies depart, are driven back, flee Lamanite attacks, and face impending overthrow.

l: city of Desolation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Desolation is a city by a narrow pass in the land Desolation. Nephite armies defend it against Lamanites, who capture it; the Nephites retake it, but the Lamanites capture it again amid deadly battles and Nephite defeat.

l: land of their inheritance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_given_by God [to the house of Israel] The Lord gave the land of their inheritance to the Jews, or all the house of Israel. The Father will restore them to that land through Jesus in fulfillment of the covenant.

l: earth, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Mormon wrote to all the ends of the earth and testified that the unrepentant Nephites would be cut off from the face of the earth. The earth was created by the word of God. In the day of visitation, it will be rolled together as a scroll and its elements will melt with fervent heat.

l: armies, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_a military forces [of the Nephites and Lamanites] The Nephite armies were placed at the city of Desolation and fortified against the Lamanites with all their force. The Lamanite armies came to battle and were defeated.

l: Nephite victories, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: cause Nephite vengeance [through boasting in their own strength] The Nephites defeated the Lamanites in two successive years, including a battle in which many Lamanites were slain. These victories caused the Nephites to boast in their own strength.

l: Nephite vengeance, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Nephite vengeance is the promised avenging of their slain brethren: the Nephites swear to cut off their enemies, but the Lord declares vengeance belongs to him and that he will repay those responsible.

l: prayer, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_offered_to the Father (God) [in the name of Jesus Christ] People are instructed to cry mightily unto the Father in the name of Jesus and to ask for whatever they need. The prayers of the saints concern the restoration of the brethren to the knowledge of Christ.

l: judgment, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The judgment is an event after the resurrection, at the judgment-seat of Christ, when every soul of Adam’s family stands to be judged by works, good or evil. Israel and the Nephite remnant are judged by twelve chosen by Jesus. The dead become incorruptible; the guiltless dwell with God, while the filthy and righteous remain eternally in their states.

l: gospel of Jesus Christ, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The gospel of Jesus Christ is a message known by the scriptures, available among Gentiles, and set before a remnant in records from Jews and Gentiles. Mormon urges the ends of the earth to believe it, while another witness affirms that Jesus is the Christ and God. The gospel goes from Gentiles to the seed of the people to strengthen belief, calls people to lay hold on it, and is preached to every creature; believers who are baptized are saved.

l: Jews, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The unbelieving Jews, part of the house of Israel, receive a record to persuade them that Jesus is the Christ; through Jesus, the Father will restore them to their inherited land.

l: human family of Adam, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_judged_by Jesus Christ [according to works, whether good or evil] Every soul belonging to the whole human family of Adam must stand before the judgment-seat of Christ and be judged according to its works.

l: Adam, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Adam, ancestor of the human family, is created by God and causes the fall of man.

l: city Teancum, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: City Teancum, near the seashore and city Desolation, repulses Lamanites before they expel inhabitants and take many prisoners.

l: sacrifices of women and children, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Lamanites take Nephite women and children prisoner, sacrifice them to idol gods, provoking Nephites to defeat and temporarily drive them out.

l: seed of Jacob, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The seed of Jacob is a remnant scattered among the Gentiles because of unbelief and idolatry, becoming dark, filthy, and loathsome. Numbered among the people of the first covenant, it receives the gospel and may go among the Gentiles as a lion if they do not repent.

l: Satan, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: leads Nephites [as chaff driven before the wind] Satan leads the people who were once a delightsome people and had Christ for their shepherd. They are driven about by Satan as chaff before the wind or a vessel without sail, anchor, or steering.

l: covenant of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: A covenant made by the Father with Abraham and the house of Israel. After Israel is driven, scattered, and long dispersed among the Gentiles, the Lord remembers it; the text asks God to remember and bless them forever through faith on Jesus Christ.

l: destruction of the Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The destruction of the Nephites, caused by unbelief, idolatry, and failure to repent, follows defeat by the Lamanites and ends in the final battle at Cumorah. Nearly all are killed, leaving bloodshed, carnage, and remains upon the earth, causing Mormon anguish and mourning.

l: scattering of the Nephites, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_caused_by Gentiles [after the Nephites’ blessings are reserved] The Nephites are scattered by the Gentiles, and the Gentiles are said to scatter this people. Their scattering precedes the Lord's remembrance of his covenant with Abraham and all the house of Israel.

l: Lamanite invasions, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: targets Nephites [in repeated battles] The Lamanites come against the Nephites repeatedly, including attacks on the city of Jordan and other cities. Their invasions destroy lands and inhabitants that were not gathered in and eventually overwhelm the Nephite armies.

l: land of Cumorah, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Land of many waters, rivers, and fountains, containing hill Cumorah, where the Nephites gather for their final battle.

l: hill Cumorah, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: contains records [hidden there by Mormon] The hill Cumorah is the location around which the Nephites pitch their tents and from which the survivors view the slain. Mormon hides the records entrusted to him in the hill Cumorah.

l: battle, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The final battle at Cumorah is fought with swords, bows, arrows, axes, and other weapons of war. The Lamanites overwhelm the Nephites, killing nearly all of them.

l: records, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Sacred records, entrusted to Mormon, are kept from the Lamanites, who would destroy them; Mormon hides them in hill Cumorah and gives a few plates to Moroni.

l: Moroni, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Moroni, Mormon’s son and a descendant of Nephi, survives with twenty-four others and receives plates from Mormon. After his people’s destruction, he remains alone, finishes and keeps Mormon’s record, warns future people against pride and oppression, then writes and hides the records in the earth despite lacking ore for plates.

l: death, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: has_sting_swallowed_up Jesus Christ [in him] In Jesus Christ, the sting of death is swallowed up. Jesus Christ has gained the victory over the grave.

l: twenty and four survivors, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Twenty and four Nephite survivors remain with Mormon after the Lamanites slay the Nephites, including his son Moroni.

l: anguish and mourning, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: is_experienced_by Mormon [because of the slain Nephites] Mormon's soul is rent with anguish because of the slain Nephites. He cries out in mourning over their rejection of Jesus and laments that his sorrows cannot bring them back.

l: Eternal Father of heaven, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Eternal Father of heaven is God, one with the Son and the Holy Ghost. He knows the dead Nephites’ state and deals with them through justice and mercy. By his power Jesus Christ was raised again. He receives prayer in Jesus Christ’s name and is asked to cleanse, grant requests, and remember his covenant with Israel.

l: war, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: War continued among the Lamanites, and no one knew when it would end.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The resurrection of the dead is brought to pass by Jesus Christ through the death of Christ, awakening all men from an endless sleep so they are raised to stand before God’s bar and the judgment-seat.

l: redemption of the world, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The redemption of the world comes through Jesus Christ. It brings all men into the presence of the Lord through resurrection, redeeming them from temporal death. At judgment day, those found guiltless receive the presence and kingdom of God, dwell there, and sing ceaseless praises.

l: Son, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: The Son is Jesus Christ, one God with the Father and Holy Ghost, through whom man’s redemption came; the guiltless praise him, and he commands disciples to preach with promised signs.

l: record, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Chapter 7 says the record contains Christ’s gospel, enabling belief, knowledge of ancestors and God’s works, and bringing belief to Gentiles and a remnant.

l: covenant people of the Lord, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: are house of Israel [as a covenant people] The covenant people of the Lord are the house of Israel. Those who oppose the Lord’s work and seek to destroy them are in danger of being hewn down and cast into the fire.

l: baptism, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Baptism is commanded by Jesus Christ and required for salvation for believers. It begins with water, then fire and the Holy Ghost, following the Savior’s example. People are told to be baptized in Jesus’s name, warned against unworthy baptism, and taught that believers baptized shall be saved.

l: salvation, The Book of Mormon, Mormon's Own Record
s: Salvation requires repentance and is unavailable without it; it is received by those who believe and are baptized. People must work it out with fear and trembling, live worthily, and endure to the end to avoid being cast out.
